name: Hashcat - Crack NetNTLMv2 Hash
description: Cracks captured NetNTLMv2 hashes (Hashcat mode 5600) offline to recover plaintext passwords. NetNTLMv2 hashes cannot be used for pass-the-hash — cracking is the only path to leveraging them. Significantly faster with GPU.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHY NTLMV2 MUST BE CRACKED (NOT PTH'd) ===
NTLMv2 is a challenge-response mechanism: the authenticating client proves knowledge
of the NT hash by computing HMAC-MD5(NTHash, challenge). The output (the hash you
captured) is DIFFERENT every session because the challenge changes. It cannot replay
against any service. You must find the original plaintext.

=== HASH FORMAT ===
NTLMv2 hash captured by Responder:
  USER::DOMAIN:ServerChallenge:NTProofStr:blob
  e.g.: backupagent::INLANEFREIGHT:4a8a02...:d2f3...:0101000000...
This full string is what goes in your hash file. Don't truncate it.

=== HASHCAT MODES ===
  5600  = NTLMv2  (NetNTLM challenge-response — what Responder captures)
  5500  = NTLMv1  (older, rarer, weaker — less common in modern environments)
  1000  = NTLM    (the raw NT hash — NOT what Responder captures)

=== CRACKING STRATEGY ===
1. rockyou.txt first (fastest): hashcat -m 5600 hash.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
2. Rules on rockyou: hashcat -m 5600 hash.txt rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
3. Larger wordlists: /usr/share/seclists/Passwords/
4. Masks for corporate patterns: hashcat -m 5600 hash.txt -a 3 ?u?l?l?l?l?d?d?s

=== WHAT TO EXPECT ===
User account hashes: often crack if the user chose a weak/common password
Machine account (HOSTNAME$) hashes: almost never crack (random 120-char passwords)
Service account hashes: frequently weak (admins set them and never rotate)

=== AFTER CRACKING ===
You have a plaintext password. Use it to:
  1. Spray across other systems (same user may reuse)
  2. Access the specific service the hash was captured from
  3. Get NT hash via secretsdump if you can authenticate with it
  4. Try Evil-WinRM if the user has WinRM access

=== IF THE HASH DOESN'T CRACK ===
Consider NTLM relay instead (ntlmrelayx.py) — relay the captured challenge-response
directly to a target service without needing the plaintext.

defense.why_it_works: The NetNTLMv2 hash captured from poisoning is a challenge-response derived from the user's password, so it can be cracked offline with a wordlist.
defense.prerequisites: Captured NetNTLM hashes and a wordlist.
defense.impact: Plaintext passwords from poisoned authentications - initial access or lateral movement.
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1110.002 M1027] Long, high-entropy passwords make the offline NetNTLM crack infeasible; the hash is already captured, so the victim cannot detect the cracking - password strength is the only defence.
defense.misconfiguration: LLMNR (Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution, UDP 5355) and NBT-NS (NetBIOS Name Service, UDP 137) are enabled by default on Windows and are used as fallback name resolution when DNS fails. These protocols broadcast name queries on the local network segment. Any host on the same subnet can respond to these broadcasts — a Responder instance claims to be the queried host and captures the NTLMv2 hash when the victim tries to authenticate.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# LLMNR enabled (Windows default):
# Registry: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient
#   EnableMulticast: (not set or 1) = LLMNR active

# NBT-NS enabled (Windows default):
# Network adapter -> TCP/IP properties -> WINS -> 'Enable NetBIOS over TCP/IP'
# = Default (or Enabled)

# Test: trigger a failed DNS lookup, watch Responder capture NTLMv2:
# net use \\nonexistent  -> host broadcasts LLMNR for 'nonexistent'
# Responder replies -> host sends NTLMv2 -> Responder captures it
defense.secure_config:
# Disable LLMNR via GPO:
# Computer Config > Admin Templates > Network > DNS Client
#   'Turn off multicast name resolution' = Enabled
# OR Registry:
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient' \
    -Name EnableMulticast -Value 0

# Disable NBT-NS via GPO (push WMI script or DHCP option 001 = 0x2):
# Or per-machine:
Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapterConfiguration | ForEach-Object {
    $_.SetTcpipNetbios(2)  # 2 = Disable NetBIOS
}

# Enable SMB signing (stops relay attacks even if hash captured):
Set-SmbServerConfiguration -RequireSecuritySignature $true -Force

# Deploy a honeypot LLMNR responder for detection
# Sysmon/IDS: alert on Responder-like traffic (UDP 5355 responses from non-DC hosts)
defense.evasion: Run analyze-only first to gauge traffic; poison selectively (specific names) rather than everything; short windows reduce the chance a defender notices spoofed responses.
